title: Above their department
prompt: Show the name of employees earning more than their own department's average. Replace the ___.
hints: Link the inner query with x.department_id = e.department_id.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(x.salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(x.salary) FROM employees x);
SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.salary < (SELECT AVG(x.salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id);

title: Top price per category
prompt: Show the name and price of the most expensive product in each category.
hints: Compare with MAX within the same category.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT p.name, p.price FROM products p WHERE p.price = (SELECT MAX(x.price) FROM products x WHERE x.category = p.category);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.name, p.price FROM products p WHERE p.price = (SELECT MAX(x.price) FROM products x);
SELECT p.name, p.price FROM products p WHERE p.price = (SELECT MIN(x.price) FROM products x WHERE x.category = p.category);

title: Latest order per customer
prompt: Show each customer_id and order_date for that customer's most recent order.
hints: Compare each order with that customer's MAX date.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_date FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MAX(x.order_date) FROM orders x WHERE x.customer_id = o.customer_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_date FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MAX(x.order_date) FROM orders x);
SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_date FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MIN(x.order_date) FROM orders x WHERE x.customer_id = o.customer_id);

title: Best in course
prompt: Show the student_id and grade of the top grade in each course, including ties.
hints: Compare each grade with the course's MAX.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

title: Earlier hire exists
prompt: Show the name of employees for whom someone in the same department was hired earlier.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id AND x.hire_date < e.hire_date);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees x WHERE x.hire_date < e.hire_date);
SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id AND x.hire_date < e.hire_date);

title: Above-average orders per customer
prompt: Show the customer_id and order id as order_id of orders with more units than that customer's average order.
hints: Compute order totals with a subquery, used on both sides.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT t.customer_id, t.order_id FROM (SELECT o.customer_id, i.order_id, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id, i.order_id) t WHERE t.units > (SELECT AVG(y.units) FROM (SELECT o.customer_id, i.order_id, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id, i.order_id) y WHERE y.customer_id = t.customer_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT t.customer_id, t.order_id FROM (SELECT o.customer_id, i.order_id, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id, i.order_id) t;

SELECT t.customer_id, t.order_id FROM (SELECT o.customer_id, i.order_id, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id, i.order_id) t WHERE t.units > (SELECT AVG(quantity) FROM order_items);
